notes: DISPATCH 3 (2026-08-24) — THE SINGLE-DIE PLACEMENT WALL WAS NOT REAL; the block now PLACES, ROUTES and FLOWS on one die, but is NOT yet bit-exact, so the outcome stays needs_human. WHAT THE PRIOR ANALYSIS GOT WRONG (both walls were layout convention, not fabric): (a) 'a stage cannot spill out of its 2-row band' is the PARITY THEOREM seen through one rectangle — a chain of L cells can land its LAST cell edge-adjacent to its FIRST only when L is EVEN (chessboard colouring; proven here by exhaustive search over all self-avoiding walks for L=2..12). The repair is a delay-line pad spreading the SAME total delay over one extra cell: 81 -> 84 cells, 3 of 6 stages padded. (b) the 11-row budget assumed a 10-WIDE fold; a fold whose spine column avoids the port columns may use ROW 0, so the array gives 12 rows and N=64's 6-stage spine needs exactly 12. THE REAL GEOMETRY (measured, and it is what FFT16 already does): a stage's out cell needs THREE @1 neighbours — its own ctl directly ABOVE (write-back + lock-clear on face_fb=NORTH), the NEXT stage's ctl directly BELOW (forward packet on face_tap=SOUTH, which is ALSO the resting face and therefore what the router traces), and for the last stage a free neighbour for the egress. So the ctl/out sequence is ONE COLUMN of 2*n_stages cells. Everything ELSE in a stage is free to bulge sideways — which is precisely what the band scheme forbade and what makes N=64 fit. THE TRAP THAT HID IT: a bad internal hop does NOT error. router._get_routing_distance traces resting faces and SILENTLY falls back to Manhattan distance, so a non-traceable inter-stage handoff ships a wrong hop and the stage spins on its own ring (measured: stage 0 alone burned 1e6 simulator events and stage 1 never ran). Turned into a static gate: trace every forward internal edge and compare with its chain distance — FFT16 scores 0/188, the shipped fold 0/349. FOLD STRATEGIES TRIED: (1) per-stage RING FOLD (a boustrophedon generalising FFT16's 2-row band to R rows, out landing below ctl) shelf-packed side by side — 84 cells in 10 rows, but REJECTED on chip: out faced its own ctl so the inter-stage packets were untraceable and stage 0 livelocked. (2) the same with a general HAMILTONIAN ring search per box — found face-clean walks, but they zig-zag between two columns and crowd the ring; also livelocked. A walk that is 'clean by the stated rule' is not the same as one that behaves like the shipped block. (3) wide-box-only ring folds — still livelocked, which is what forced the correct diagnosis. (4) the VERTICAL CTL/OUT SPINE that shipped: stages placed by a backtracking self-avoiding-path search around a fixed spine column, with a corridor-reachability check (a fold that FILLS the array builds and then fails to route — 'no free corridor between the ports') and an exit-face rule (the last out must NOT rest toward its own ctl, or it re-enters the stage instead of leaving the block). VERIFIED ON A REAL BUILT CHIP: places at anchor (0,0), both nets route with real corridors (input 5 cells, egress 17), build ok, and driving it executes ALL 84 cells with per-stage activity decreasing monotonically s0->s5 — 3.2k events per burst against the 1e6 runaway of the rejected folds. 51 gates green in test_fft64_fit_limit.py (37 arithmetic + 11 spine-structural + 3 INV-4 mutations proven to FAIL on corrupted layouts); FFT16's 37 unregressed. NOT DONE, PLAINLY: only the FIRST sample's output word egresses. Sample 1 enters s0_ctl, runs stage 0 as far as s0_mcalc, and s0_tab_c onward never execute; by sample 2 the input corridor is back-pressured and the chip goes quiescent. RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT: the serialize-LOCK clear (the out->ctl write-back is patched to hop 1 via the direct-abutment branch, byte-for-byte as FFT16), the loaded bitstream (s0_mcalc's on-chip image equals its resolved image; entry 8 = 0x9823; BOTH branch paths end in the same jump trig = hop 1 to its EAST neighbour, which is where s0_tab_c actually sits), and the placement/faces/hops (all audits clean). ROOT CAUSE FOUND (and it is an ARITHMETIC bug, not a layout one): TWO CELLS OVERWRITE THEIR OWN PROGRAM. s0_mcalc has entry address 8 and its StateVar t resolves to register 8; s1_fetch_d has entry 21 and ptr resolves to 21. The first MOVE R{state:..}, R0 zeroes the instruction the NEXT trigger enters at, so sample 1 enters a HALT and the pipeline dies. Proven by a BEFORE/AFTER memory dump of the stalling cell (address 8 goes 0x9823 -> 0x0000 during sample 0). This is INV-33 exactly - state auto-allocates into range(max_data_address+1, 31-instr_count) and both cells are EXACTLY full at 31/32 words, so that range collides with the instruction region. THE TRAP FOR THE NEXT BUILDER: the prior dispatch gated the 32-WORD COUNT and passed; the word count is fine, it is the OVERLAP that is fatal, and a self-overwriting cell presents exactly like a serialize-LOCK failure (runs once, then dead) while surviving every placement/face/hop audit. A new gate, test_no_cell_overwrites_its_own_program, catches it and is currently a STRICT xfail so it flips the moment the cells are fixed. The fix is to free one word in each cell by re-deriving its arithmetic and re-verifying against the fold golden - every data word in both is genuinely used, so a re-pin alone cannot work. NOT attempted here rather than guessed at: changing the cell math without re-verifying it is how a silently-wrong block ships. No on-chip bit-exactness, SNR, GRC binding, saturation or orientation gates yet: all downstream of that fix.
